AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To evaluate the overall health-related quality of life in patients with bronchiolitis obliterans.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Participants with a diagnosis of post-infectious bronchiolitis obliterans (PIBO), who were being followed-up at two specialized outpatient clinics of Pediatric Pulmonology in Porto Alegre, Brazil, and controls aged between 8 and 17 years, of both genders, were included in the study. Controls were paired by gender, age, and socioeconomic level in relation to the group of participants with PIBO. The version of the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQ) tool validated for Brazil was applied for the assessment of Health-related Quality of Life (HRQoL), through an interview. The comparison of the HRQoL means between the groups was performed using Student's t-test for independent samples and the chi-squared test, for categorical variables.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: 34 patients diagnosed with PIBO and 34 controls participated in the study. The mean age of the children included in the study was 11.2±2.5 years, and 49 (72%) of them were males. The groups showed no significant differences in relation to these variables. The quality of life score was significantly and clinically lower in the PIBO group when compared with controls in the health (72.36±15.6, 81.06±16.4, p=0.031) and school domains (62.34±20.7, 72.94±21.3, p=0.043), as well as in the total score (69.53±14.9, 78.02±14.8, p=0.024), respectively.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Patients with post-infectious bronchiolitis obliterans presented lower health-related quality of life scores when compared with healthy individuals in the total score and in the health and school domains.
